A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same APC research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original interaction-log analysis, model-training evaluations, ablations, threshold experiments, and an appendix entropy analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds online interaction measurements, annotation agreement, placeholder-use statistics, and execution-based evaluations.

M1.justification: The APC strategy, SFT followed by GRPO, and cost-based reward equations remain unchanged. Added filtering and decoding descriptions document implementation details without establishing a revised method. Placeholder-symbol substitutions are not algorithmic changes.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's observational log analysis and offline evaluations, v2 adds a live HC-only versus APC interaction scenario covering a reported 1.8 million interactions. This substantially extends evaluation into deployed human interaction. HumanEval Infilling and the curated PC benchmark remain; adding Pass@1 does not introduce another dataset.

E2.justification: All identified offline comparators are retained, and the new Pass@1 comparison reuses Base/SFT/GRPO. However, the online control is identified only as 'HC-only,' without its model or training configuration. The PDFs do not establish whether it introduces a distinct comparator or reuses an earlier baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 introduces an online A/B evaluation with 1.2 million HC-only and 0.6 million APC interactions, measuring editing actions, reading/editing time, and output length. Appendix F adds sandbox execution and Pass@1 evaluation. Existing training/test counts remain unchanged; Appendix G's decoding settings are newly disclosed, not demonstrated setting changes.

E4.justification: New Appendices D, E, and H add descriptive cost-ratio estimates, placeholder-frequency/output-length diagnostics, and illustrative Flask and business-logic cases. Existing data/reward ablations and threshold sweeps remain unchanged. The entropy analysis moves from v1 Appendix D to v2 Section 5.4 rather than constituting a new analysis.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports reciprocal cross-annotation on a PC-benchmark subset and inter-annotator reliability using Fleiss' Kappa, obtaining 0.7994. The subset size and annotator count are unspecified. No repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 and ablation-table values are unchanged. New Table 2 reports HC-only/APC cursor moves of 4.89/3.06 and reading/editing times of 3280.49/2255.17 ms. Table 6 adds Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct Pass@1 results: Base/SFT/GRPO score 0.5798/0.6621/0.8315 for single-line and 0.3745/0.4368/0.5958 for multi-line infilling. Annotation agreement and placeholder-use statistics are also new results, not improvements over corresponding v1 measurements.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, theorem, corollary, derivations, and Appendix B proofs retain their mathematical content. v2 discusses the existing uniform-distribution assumption more explicitly but supplies no revised theorem or proof. Changes to placeholder notation are equivalent.

C1.justification: The conclusion adds an explicit claim of 31–37% reductions in measured editing actions and time, and describes the entropy threshold as motivation for learning rather than as directly delineating optimal strategy selection. The abstract and introduction retain the principal APC contributions and existing cost-reduction claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and limitations: non-uniform real-world token distributions, ES failing to capture semantic error severity, dependence on interactive IDE navigation, and annotator-induced distributional bias. It also attributes Pass@1 gains to suppression of logical hallucinations and newly claims aggregate interaction ratios statistically establish the cost assumption, although no supporting significance test is reported.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly specifies temperature 0.1, top-p 0.95, and 256 maximum new tokens. Appendix E describes placeholder-density filtering, giving a one-third limit as an example. The impact statement replaces a general future sanitization commitment with reported PII redaction and fuzzy deduplication. These disclosures do not establish rerunning existing experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography are unchanged. APC's stated relationship to prior code completion, abstention, skeleton generation, and reinforcement-learning approaches remains the same.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized rewrites to the theory-to-practice discussion, Section 5.3, conclusion, and impact statement; corrects wording and placeholder notation; and moves the entropy appendix into Section 5.4. New experimental and appendix sections extend the existing structure, while most original prose and organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with an introductory APC schematic, tables for online interactions, placeholder use, Pass@1, and decoding settings, plus boxed qualitative examples. The existing entropy figure moves from a full-width appendix display to a smaller main-text figure. Original benchmark and ablation displays retain their contents.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful interaction measurements and execution-based correctness evidence beyond v1's proxy and string metrics, alongside clearer limitations and decoding details. However, the online models and allocation procedure are underspecified, its interaction count conflicts between Section 4.3 and Appendix D (1.8 versus 1.6 million), and Appendix D unjustifiably treats aggregate averages as statistical proof of the per-error cost assumption. The additions improve empirical relevance and transparency, but these reporting and inference problems limit the overall gain.
